subject: Private deployment: custodian roles & data egress constraints

Subject: Private deployment – key custody and subprocessors

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the product overview last week. As we evaluate Redwood’s private/VPC deployment for Aurora Health, a few security and legal items came up we need clarity on before procurement:

- Customer-controlled keys: can customers bring their own KMS (HSM-backed) and fully control rotation/deletion without Redwood having an escrow copy?
- Operator access: what operator actions (if any) can Redwood perform inside a private deployment? Is there a documented breakglass procedure?
- Subprocessors: can you provide a current subprocessor list and a standard notification window for additions?
- Cross-border/data transfer: does any telemetry, usage metrics, or exception reporting leave our VPC/region? If so, what’s contained and is it encrypted with our key?

Appreciate a short written summary and any DPA or SOW examples you can share — our legal and procurement leads are on copy.

Regards,
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Security, Aurora Health

Subject: Re: Private deployment – key custody and subprocessors

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: customer-managed KMS is supported in VPC/private deploys; Redwood does not retain a plaintext copy of customer keys; operator access is tightly scoped and breakglass is documented; telemetry can be limited and encrypted under customer keys.

I attached a copy of our standard private-deploy DPA and an initial SOW stub for procurement (redwood_private_dpa_v1.pdf, aurora_sow_draft.docx).

I’ve looped in Markus (security) and Priyom (SE) to add technical detail and a suggested subprocessor list. Would you be available for a 45-minute call Monday to walk through the breakglass sequence and key-handover steps?

Next steps we propose:
- Quick call to confirm KMS model (Cloud KMS vs. in-cluster HSM) and acceptable breakglass approval flow
- Provide current subprocessor list and SOC2 summaries
- Redline DPA with Aurora’s legal changes (we can accept limited escrow terms if mutually agreeable)

Thanks — talk soon.

Cheers,

Subject: Re: Private deployment – key custody and subprocessors

Sarah — adding the technical specifics you’ll need for procurement and security review. See inline answers.

1) Customer KMS options
- We support customer-managed keys via Cloud KMS (AWS KMS with custom key policy) or an on-prem HSM reachable from the Redwood runtime via TLS and client auth.
- Redwoods’ runtime never stores key material in plaintext. We accept asymmetric signing/ wrapping keys or use an external KMS plugin for decrypt operations.

2) Key rotation and escrow
- Customer retains authority over rotation. Redwood supports on-demand key rotation flows but does not automatically rotate your master key.
- Escrow: by default no escrow; if a customer requires key escrow for contractual reasons we support a split-keystore escrow mechanism with customer approval workflows (requires separate addendum).

3) Operator access & breakglass
- Operator actions in private deployments are restricted to: emergency patching, startup/shutdown of runtime, and controlled troubleshooting.
- All operator actions are recorded with cryptographic audit logs (timestamps, operator identity).
- Breakglass: we require documented POA + two approvals from our on-call SRE lead and the security manager; actions are read-only by default except when decrypt access is explicitly granted and audited.

4) Telemetry & egress
- Usage telemetry is configurable. Default private deployment config sends subsetted, encrypted telemetry (error hashes, perf counters) to Redwood monitoring endpoints. We can disable telemetry to external endpoints; alternatively telemetry can be forwarded to a customer-owned collector in your VPC and encrypted under your key.

5) Subprocessors and notice
- Core subprocessors: metrics collector (Datadog), logging pipeline (S3 signed buckets), support ticketing (Zendesk). Full list attached (subprocessor_list_202605.pdf).
- Standard notice window for processor additions is 30 days; can be negotiated to 60 for enterprise customers.

I attached the subprocessor list and SOC2 summary snippets. Happy to cover the HSM integration in Monday’s call.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Security Engineering, Redwood Inference

Forwarding Markus’ note to our legal and procurement team. A couple of clarifying items from our side:

- Key rotation: do you require any API callbacks to Redwood when keys are rotated or revoked? We prefer no external dependency.
- HSM vs Cloud KMS: if we host an on-prem HSM reachable only over the private network, will Redwood need to provision any credentials that we can’t revoke?

Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood DPA — proposed redlines and audit requests

Chloe / Lauren — I reviewed the draft DPA Chloe sent. A few legal items we’d like Redwood to accept or clarify before countersigning:

1) Subprocessor notice: propose minimum 45-day written notice for subprocessor additions that affect processing of Aurora data; requirement of right to object and for Redwood to provide mitigation/termination assistance if objection is valid.
2) Audit and attestations: we need SOC2 Type II copies for the specific environment or the option for a scoped audit once a quarter for the pilot period.
3) Key escrow: if Redwood requests any escrow, we need the escrow architecture documented and an escrow-only key custody policy; otherwise we prefer zero escrow.
4) Data export & egress: require explicit clause that telemetry or exception traces sent off-premise will be encrypted with Aurora-controlled keys and enumerated in Schedule X; any exception must be preapproved by Aurora security.

I can circulate redlines to the PDF; also request a short timeline for incorporation and a call with Redwood legal to finalize.

-Jonathan Chen
Partner, Legal Partners LLP
From: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Chen <jonathan.chen@legalpartners.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@auroramed.com>, Alex White <alex.white@auroramed.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — proposed redlines and audit requests

Thanks Jonathan — and thanks Aurora team for the detailed feedback. Proposed path forward below (we can turn these into formal redlines and a DocuSign packet by EOD):

- Subprocessor notice: Redwood accepts a 30-day notice by default and will accept 45 days for Aurora as an enterprise term. We’ll add the right to object and provide termination assistance language in the DPA redline.
- SOC2 / audits: we will provide scoped SOC2 Type II artifacts for the private deployment instance. For extra assurance during the pilot, we can provide a quarterly scoped attestation or a scoped audit at Aurora’s cost.
- Key escrow/custody: default remains zero-escrow — customer retains full control. If escrow is required, we’ll use the split-keystore model with escrow only after mutual written agreement and a separate addendum.
- Telemetry & egress: we will add a binding Schedule stating telemetry defaults to customer-owned collector in the VPC (no external egress) when Aurora enables that option. Any telemetry that would leave the VPC must be encrypted with Aurora’s key and preapproved.
- Breakglass: define POA + 2-approver workflow; all actions logged and reversible where feasible.

Next steps:
1) I’ll circulate redlined DPA and an updated subprocessor list by EOD (attached: redwood_dpa_redline_20260505.pdf).
2) If Aurora is good with the 45-day notice and the telemetry schedule, we’ll open a DocuSign envelope for the SOW + DPA and aim for a pilot start within 3 weeks of signature. DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/aurora/AUR-PL-2026-SOW
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive Wednesday to confirm HSM connectivity and KMS API flows (I’ll work with Priyom on time selection).

Please confirm the DocuSign/PO timeline and whether Aurora wants the scoped audit or attestations for the pilot.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Sr. Manager, Solutions & Privacy
Redwood Inference
